verdicts.title: Optimizer-state restore silently degrades to template defaults when the optimizer or parameter set changes across a resume
verdicts.reasoning: Reproduced at library level with uv run: an adamw chain state stepped 3 times serialises to {'[0].mu.*','[0].nu.*','[0].phi','[0].step'}; from_state_dict(lion.init(params), adam_sd) is accepted and yields LionState(step=3) with an all-zero momentum buffer (printed 'Adam sd -> Lion template ACCEPTED: LionState step= 3 m all-zero: True'). The subset case also reproduces: a 2-parameter Adam snapshot restored into a 3-parameter template gives mu['c'] max = 0.0 while mu['w'] restores to 0.135, step = 3. Mechanism verified in source: opaque-engine/.../serialization/_structural.py:65-73 `_tensor_load` does `saved = sd.get(""); if saved is None: return template`, and opaque-base/.../_structural.py:110-112 `walk_load` on a Mapping iterates only the template's keys, so extra saved keys are dropped and missing ones silently fall back. '[0].step' is a shared key name, which is why the step counter does carry over from the wrong optimizer. Trainer reachability verified by reading: _dp_trainer.py:5559-5567 loads dp_optimizer.pt and calls opaque_from_state_dict(ctx.opt_state, opt_sd) unconditionally, and RuntimeCheckpoint (_checkpoint.py:227-303) has no `optim` field among the compare_on_resume entries, so no drift warning or error fires. The DP trainer has its own resume path (DP_OPTIMIZER_NAME), so HF's optimizer.pt mismatch checks never run either. Caveats that cap severity: the tolerance is documented and deliberate (from_state_dict docstring: 'missing leaves keep the template's value (forward compatibility when new fields appear)'), shape mismatches ARE caught by _check_shape, this is a user-error path (you must change `optim` or the trainable-parameter set between phases), and the consequence is training-trajectory/utility only - no privacy state is involved and epsilon is unaffected. I did not execute a full trainer resume with a changed `optim`; the trainer link is established by code reading, not by running the trainer.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A user resumes a DPTrainer run (or a hand-managed functional chain) after changing `optim` or the trainable-parameter set. `from_state_dict` accepts the mismatched snapshot: keys that exist in both (notably '[0].step') are restored, keys only in the template are silently filled from the freshly initialised template. Verified library-level output: adamw-3-step state -> lion template gives LionState(step=3) with an all-zero momentum buffer; a 2-param snapshot -> 3-param template leaves the new parameter's mu at 0 while keeping step=3. Nothing warns, because RuntimeCheckpoint has no `optim` drift field. Effect is degraded optimizer behaviour (bias-correction/warmup state believing 3 steps have elapsed with empty moment buffers), not a privacy loss; epsilon is unchanged.

verdicts.title: Checkpoints written by the previous release fail with unactionable errors (bare KeyError for pre-#761 k-out-of-t state, bare version number for the trainer bundle)
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified. (1) `git show fc44ec8d^:.../_k_out_of_t.py` shows the pre-#761 persisted keys were key_seed/key_impl/consumed/num_samples/total_participations/n_steps; the current _state_dict_k_out_of_t (_k_out_of_t.py:179-188) writes k/t/allocation instead. (2) _from_state_dict_k_out_of_t guards num_samples with a full ConfigurationError (lines 196-203) but then does `saved = state[name]` for name in ('k','t','allocation') at 204-212 with no key guard. Ran the reproduction under uv: 'old k_out_of_t sd REJECTED: KeyError : k'. (3) load_dp_runtime_state (_checkpoint.py:399-405) raises CheckpointError(f'unsupported dp_state bundle version {bundle.version} (expected {DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION})') with DP_STATE_BUNDLE_VERSION = 8 and no statement of which release wrote the old version or what to do. (4) packages/opaque-base/src/opaque/api/base/serialization/_compat.py is still an empty placeholder ('Reserved for future use', __all__ = []). (5) No CHANGELOG file at the repo root and no migration page under docs/ (docs/limitations.md says nothing about checkpoint portability). Two things cap severity and slightly overstate the finding's own framing: both failures are fail-closed hard errors - no silent wrong resume, no epsilon impact - and release notes do exist outside the tree (cliff.toml drives generated GitHub Release bodies), so 'no way to learn' is too strong; what is genuinely missing is the up-front key-set validation and the writing-release identity in the message. This is an error-message/ergonomics defect, not a correctness one.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: Resuming a checkpoint written by an earlier release fails with a message that does not name the cause or the remedy. Verified: a pre-#761 k-out-of-t snapshot (total_participations/n_steps) raises a bare `KeyError: 'k'` because _from_state_dict_k_out_of_t indexes state['k'], state['t'], state['allocation'] without a guard, even though the adjacent num_samples check raises a fully explanatory ConfigurationError. A pre-version-8 trainer bundle raises `CheckpointError: unsupported dp_state bundle version N (expected 8)` naming neither the writing release nor the fact that migration is unsafe. Both are fail-closed - the run stops rather than resuming wrongly - so there is no privacy or correctness impact; the cost is operator time. The designated versioning seam (opaque/api/base/serialization/_compat.py) is still empty and there is no in-tree CHANGELOG or migration page.

verdicts.title: Applied-vs-reported noise magnitude is untested on four sibling noise paths (the OPQ-378/#833 conformance test covers only the scalar DP-SGD path)
verdicts.reasoning: Independently reproduced for three of the four paths with runtime-only mutations (I did not edit the repository; I injected the defect from a pytest plugin, so the working tree stayed clean - `git status` empty before and after). Mutation A/C: a plugin patched PerGroup.for_path to return 0.95x ONLY when the immediate caller frame is the draw helper (`_add_noise_tree` in opaque-dpsgd _gaussian.py, `_iid_normal_noise` in opaque-dpftrl _engine.py), leaving reported metadata untouched. Sanity check confirmed the injection is exact: reported 2.4495 vs realized 2.3282 (ratio 0.9505) and reported 5.4772 vs realized 5.2045 (ratio 0.9502). With it installed, `pytest -m 'not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed'` over packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests packages/opaque-engine/tests tests/ => 2130 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed; a serial run over the three noise/clipping test dirs reported 'MUTATION draw-side sigma lookups scaled: 144' with 484 passed, proving the mutation was live and undetected. Mutation D: a plugin wrapped _adaptive._sample_noisy_clipping_rate (also rebound in _distributed) to draw with 0.95*fraction_noise_std => 'MUTATION adaclip noise draws scaled: 592', 1523 passed, 26 skipped, 0 failed, matching the finding's own M14 numbers. Path B (paired second moment) I verified by inspection rather than mutation: the second-stddev value reaches the draw as a plain float, so no surgical runtime injection was available; packages/opaque-dpsgd/tests/noise/test_gaussian_second_moment.py and packages/opaque-dpftrl/tests/noise/test_second_moment_noise.py contain no .std()/.var()/square() at all, and test_paired_noise_stddevs.py asserts only reported values (pytest.approx on noise_stddev and the Mahalanobis identity). Coverage claims checked directly: the only per-group magnitude assertion in dpsgd is the scale-invariant ratio `assert mlp_var > attn_var * 2.5` on 100 samples (test_per_group_noise.py:48-50); the dpftrl per-group file has no realized statistic; the absolute-std assertions in test_gaussian_compute_dtype.py all use scalar max_norm and so take the tree_map branch, not the PerGroup branch; the OPQ-378 conformance tests (test_noise.py:133-142 and dpftrl test_realized_stddev.py:41-48,136-155) use a scalar max_norm only. Epsilon consequence reproduced with opaque's own accountant: poisson(gaussian(nm), sample_rate=0.01).repeated_pld(1000).epsilon_at(delta=1e-5) = 1.828321647525279 at nm=1.0, 2.0429887159414375 at nm=0.95 (+11.7%), 1.9335743915236208 at the nm=0.974039 the paired-stream case implies - matching the finding's figures exactly. My adaclip epsilon spot-check used a different step count and gave a smaller relative gap (+7.7%) than the finding's +13.7%, so treat that one number as setup-dependent. Severity: this is a latent test-coverage gap, not a live defect - today's code draws the right sigma - which is why it is medium, not high; it is not tracked by any open issue (#348 'Add mechanism-to-accountant conformance tests', whose acceptance criteria were exactly 'every supported DP-SGD noise path has a corresponding conformance case' and 'a deliberate scale mismatch makes the suite fail', is CLOSED as completed, and its scope explicitly named AdaClip).
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: A 5% shortfall between the noise actually drawn and the sigma the accountant is charged for passes the entire non-CUDA suite on four shipped draw sites. Independently reproduced with runtime-injected mutations at HEAD: (a) per-group DP-SGD Gaussian and (c) per-group MF/DP-FTRL - scaling the draw-side PerGroup sigma lookup by 0.95 (144 lookups scaled, verified realized/reported ratio 0.950) leaves 2130 tests across opaque-dpsgd, opaque-dpftrl, opaque-engine and tests/ green; (d) AdaClip quantile noise - drawing with 0.95*fraction_noise_std (592 draws) leaves 1523 tests green. (b) the paired second-moment stream has no realized-magnitude assertion anywhere (its tests use torch.zeros(10) and assert only reported metadata), verified by inspection rather than mutation. The only per-group magnitude assertion in the tree is a scale-invariant ratio on 100 samples. Cost if such a regression lands: for a uniform 5% per-group shortfall, a run reported at eps=1.8283 (q=0.01, 1000 steps, delta=1e-5) actually delivers eps=2.0430 (+11.7%), measured with opaque's own accountant; the paired-stream variant implies an effective nm of 0.974 and eps=1.9336. No current miscalibration is claimed - the defect is that the guard which was added for the scalar path (#833) was never extended to its four siblings.

verdicts.title: A GPU runner with <24 GB silently skips the entire Triton kernel suite and the CUDA lane still reports green
verdicts.reasoning: Every link verified at HEAD. (1) packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels/conftest.py:20-48 - MIN_KERNEL_CUDA_MEM_GB = 24; pytest_collection_modifyitems returns early only if CUDA is absent or total_memory >= 24 GiB, then attaches pytest.mark.skip to EVERY collected item whose resolved path is relative to the kernels directory. There is no stress/perf predicate; the in-code comment scopes the skip to the directory (correctly preventing repo-wide skipping) but calls that directory 'the kernel stress suite', which it is not. (2) Functional proof executed: loading that conftest, stubbing torch.cuda.is_available()->True and get_device_properties()->16 GiB, and feeding it one item per kernels test file plus one dpsgd item marks 19/19 kernel files and 0 outside items, reason 'Kernel stress tests require >= 24GB CUDA memory (found 16.00GB).' (3) Collection counts match the finding exactly: `pytest --collect-only -m 'cuda and not slow' packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels` -> 225/397 collected (397 total). Those 19 files are the numerical suite (test_kernel_precision, test_rms_norm, test_swiglu, test_geglu, test_rope, test_cross_entropy, test_linear_cross_entropy, test_lora, MoE, autocast, compile...), not just perf cases. (4) .github/scripts/run_python_test_package.sh:38-48 - status 0 records TEST_PATH as a success and exits 0; only status 5 is special-cased, and an all-skipped run exits 0, never 5. (5) .github/scripts/assert_cuda_available.sh probes is_available(), device_count() and one tensor add - no memory assertion, so the #876/OPQ-377 preflight cannot distinguish an emptied lane from a real run. (6) .github/workflows/python-tests.yml:76-81 puts packages/opaque-patches in the 'runtime-and-patches' suite that the CUDA lanes run, and ci.yml:199-213 makes publish-dev-wheels depend on python-tests-cuda / -cuda-minimum / -cuda-latest (all on runner GPU-runner-001). Severity capped at medium because triggering requires the self-hosted runner to be re-provisioned onto a <24 GB card - it is a latent fail-open, not a currently-green-but-empty lane, and I could not inspect the live runner's card. Not a duplicate of open #880 (missing pytest.mark.cuda on two kernel files - different trigger, different files), though #880's acceptance criterion 'the CUDA lane asserting a minimum collected-test count so a silent drop to zero fails' would also fix half of this; open #774 is the umbrella for this fail-open class and would be the natural parent.
verdicts.corrected_failure_scenario: If GPU-runner-001 is re-provisioned onto a card with less than 24 GB (16 GB T4/L4/A4000 being the common case) or the label is repointed, the kernels conftest marks every item under packages/opaque-patches/tests/kernels as skipped at collection - proven functionally: 19/19 kernel test files marked, 0 items outside the directory affected, reason 'Kernel stress tests require >= 24GB CUDA memory (found 16.00GB).' That silently removes the 225 CUDA-selected tests (of 397 in the directory) that are the only validation of the fused Triton kernels, including all numerical-parity and vmap(grad) tests, not just the MELLUM perf cases the reason string names. pytest exits 0, run_python_test_package.sh records the path as a success (its only special case is exit 5), the CUDA preflight has no memory check, and all three CUDA lanes on pr.yml and ci.yml pass - so main keeps publishing dev wheels through publish-dev-wheels, which depends on exactly those jobs. This is a latent CI fail-open: it needs the runner change to fire, and no library behaviour is wrong today.
